cur:objects-coin-nikephoros-ii-basil-ii-.summary: The obverse shows the bust of Christ Pantokrator in a cross-nimbus, blessing and holding a jewelled Gospel book; on the reverse the soldier-emperor Nikephoros II Phokas and the young Basil II, the legitimate heir, hold a patriarchal cross between them. Under Nikephoros the full-weight gold coin acquired its later name, histamenon. Christ's image sanctions the partnership between the victorious general and the Macedonian dynasty.
facts: Wikipedia notes that Nikephoros II introduced a lighter gold coin, the tetarteron, after which the traditional full-weight solidus came to be called the histamenon ('standard' coin).
cur:objects-coin-nikephoros-ii-basil-ii-.notes: The file name refers to the Sear catalogue; the holding collection of this specimen is not stated on Commons.

vam:O90891.summary: At the top Christ sits in a mandorla among angels blowing trumpets, a scroll unfurled from each hand, with the archangel Michael standing on a crescent beneath him. The dead rise from their sarcophagi while their souls, in the form of doves, circle above; at the lower left an angel welcomes the clothed blessed through the gate of Heaven, and at the right the naked damned are driven into the mouth of Hell. Though the surface is now much rubbed, the carving conveys the drama of the final judgement with remarkable energy.
facts: The scroll in Christ's right hand reads VENITE BENEDICTI PATRIS MEI PERCIPITE REGNUM ('Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom', Matthew 25:34); the words to the damned on the other scroll were cut away, probably when the plaque was reused.
Unusually, Christ's left foot rests on the head of the archangel Michael. The gateway of Heaven was once inlaid with glass beads, of which a single turquoise one survives.
Around 850–870, probably near Reims, the plaque was cut down and carved on the back with the Transfiguration; it forms a pair with the V&A's Ascension plaque (254-1867).
vam:O90891.notes: The V&A relates the plaques to the ivories on the cover of the Noailles Gospels (Bibliothèque nationale de France).
